[h1][b]🎮 Reseña de CLANNAD Side Stories[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
CLANNAD Side Stories es básicamente el “álbum de historias extra” de una novela visual con fama de romperte el corazón y luego pedirte que le des las gracias. Aquí no vienes a “jugar” en el sentido tradicional: vienes a leer, escuchar una banda sonora bonita y dejar que el drama te pegue con guante blanco estilo anime.

Como Casual, cumple su promesa con una eficiencia casi insultante: cero estrés mecánico, cero reflejos, cero “skill issue”. Es el tipo de experiencia que puedes consumir con una mano en el mouse y la otra sosteniendo tu dignidad… hasta que la historia te la quite. Ideal si te gusta el romance y lo adorable con cucharadas de “¿por qué me estoy poniendo emocional por personajes dibujados?”.

Primera impresión en Steam: comunidad fantasma (0 jugadores actuales), pero con 362 recomendaciones totales. Traducido: nadie lo está jugando “ahorita”, pero los que lo jugaron, sobrevivieron lo suficiente para recomendarlo. Eso o escribieron la recomendación entre lágrimas.

[h2][b]Lo que Enamora… y lo que te deja en visto[/b][/h2]

Lo Bueno:
✅ 📖 Buena trama con enfoque en drama/romance: viene a lo que viene y no se avergüenza.  
✅ 🎼 Gran banda sonora: de esas que te hacen sentir protagonista aunque solo estés leyendo.  
✅ 🌸 Estética anime adorable: azúcar visual para que el golpe emocional entre más fácil.  
✅ 🧘‍♂️ Casual de verdad: perfecto para sesiones cortas, sin presión ni “grindeo”.  
✅ 👤 Un jugador: nadie te juzga cuando te quedas mirando la pantalla en silencio.

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 🏆 Sin logros: Steam te mira y dice “¿y tu dopamina por checklists, campeón?” 😶  
❌ 👥 0 jugadores actuales: más solo que protagonista en episodio triste 😬  
❌ 🎮 “Jugabilidad” mínima: si esperas interacción, aquí la interacción es pasar texto 📜  
❌ 🔁 Rejugabilidad limitada: si ya te sabes las historias, el impacto baja (y el drama no perdona) 🥀

Clannad Short Stories é uma novel lançada originalmente em 2010 e que depois em 2016 seria disponivilizada na Steam. Não é uma continuação da novel original como tal, é só um repertório ou coleção de histórias curtas que acontecem em momentos determinados das diferentes rotas que a novel tinha. Desse jeito, podem achar-se diversas histórias dos distintos personagens que compõem o universo da mesma novel. 

Na minha opinião são histórias que são boas, não são incríveis mas são legais. E isso é algo que deve entender-se, Clannad SS não é mais que isso e não é uma obra prima de jeito nenhum. O qual não se traduz em uma obra que seja ruim, considero que é uma carta de amor para os fãs de Clannad, serve muito se você ficou com vontade de ver um pouco mais sobre os personagens ou se tá obcecado com a VN e quer ver mais. Sua duração tampouco é algo destacável, não dá para mais de 8-9 horas ou 15 horas se você costuma cair no sono enquanto lê como eu.

Com tudo isso em conta, não sei dizer se vale a pena comprar a VN pelo preço cheio, acho que o melhor é esperar por um desconto e pronto. Entretanto, se você não pode ficar esperando então vá e compre cara, seja cara ou não no seu preço cheio, é Clannad e isso já é uma justificativa legal e razoável.

Então, bom, para concluir, em resumo posso dizer que é uma novel muito bacana e que gostei dela. Embora não seja tamanha obra prima. Acredito que sete seja uma boa nota.

P.S: Akio é foda pra caralho!

Clannad Side Stories, developed by VisualArts/Key and published by Sekai Project, serves as an affectionate companion piece to one of the most beloved visual novels ever created. Rather than acting as a sequel or an extension of the main story, this collection functions as a mosaic of short vignettes, each illuminating quieter, more personal moments from the lives of Clannad’s characters. It is a work made for fans who have already walked through the emotional journey of Tomoya and Nagisa and now wish to linger in that world a little longer—to see the small smiles, the gentle conversations, and the fleeting memories that once existed at the edges of a grander narrative. While it doesn’t aspire to replicate the sweeping drama of its predecessor, Clannad Side Stories succeeds in deepening the universe’s emotional resonance through sincerity and subtlety.

The structure of the game is immediately distinct from the traditional visual novel format. Each chapter is a self-contained short story, told in a kinetic novel style, which means there are no branching choices, no dialogue trees, and no decisions to make. The reader presses play and simply listens, reads, and absorbs the tale as it unfolds. There are sixteen of these episodes in total, each centering on a different character—some focusing on familiar faces such as Nagisa, Kyou, and Fuko, while others highlight side characters like Misae, Akio, or Yukine, who rarely stood in the spotlight before. This format brings both strengths and weaknesses. On one hand, the absence of player input allows the storytelling to flow naturally, like a series of short films, unbroken by mechanical distractions. On the other hand, it can feel limiting to those accustomed to the interactivity of a standard visual novel, and the inability to control pacing—such as skipping or pausing text freely—may frustrate players who prefer a more personalized reading rhythm.

Narratively, Clannad Side Stories offers a diverse collection of tones and moods. Some stories are lighthearted, filled with the comedic charm that once defined Clannad’s school life segments, while others delve into moments of introspection, melancholy, or nostalgia. These smaller narratives enrich the emotional fabric of the original game by showing glimpses of daily life and relationships that had been only hinted at before. They provide closure or expansion to character arcs that may have felt unfinished, and they remind players of the warmth and humanity that Key’s writing has always celebrated. None of the stories attempt to outshine the main narrative; instead, they complement it, reinforcing the sense that Clannad’s world is one where ordinary people carry extraordinary emotions beneath their simple lives. The writing, though brief in each story, carries the same blend of tenderness and humor that made the original so memorable.

The presentation of the game reflects a careful balance between familiarity and renewal. The art, handled by GotoP rather than Clannad’s original artist Itaru Hinoue, is noticeably different but still faithful to the tone of the series. Characters are drawn with softer expressions and more refined proportions, lending them a slightly modernized appearance without erasing the nostalgic aesthetic. Backgrounds are mostly static, with limited visual transitions, but this restraint emphasizes the prose and performances instead of spectacle. The music, drawn largely from the original Clannad soundtrack with a few subtle rearrangements, carries the experience beautifully. Every piece of background music feels like a faint echo from the past—a musical reminder of how deeply ingrained Clannad’s themes have become in visual novel culture.

Voice acting stands out as one of the strongest aspects of Clannad Side Stories. Every major character is fully voiced by their original actors, and the performances are filled with the same warmth, humor, and emotional authenticity that endeared these characters to players years ago. The delivery of each line helps to bridge the gap between written text and emotional resonance, particularly in scenes that would otherwise feel minimal in their visual presentation. The absence of visual dynamism is compensated by the strength of the performances, which transform each story into something closer to a radio drama or audio play. Even without complex animations, the combination of voices, music, and text successfully evokes the emotional depth that defines Key’s storytelling tradition.

While the experience is polished, its minimal interactivity may deter newcomers or casual readers. Because the stories are designed to be read linearly and automatically, the player’s role becomes purely that of an observer. This design choice is deliberate—it encourages immersion through stillness and patience—but it inevitably narrows the audience to those who already understand and appreciate Clannad’s world. For anyone unfamiliar with the characters, the context behind each scene may feel fragmented or inaccessible, as the game assumes prior emotional investment. Fans, however, will find that this very structure allows them to revisit the characters as if they were meeting old friends again, spending a few quiet hours sharing laughter and reflection rather than embarking on another dramatic journey.

In terms of length and pacing, the collection can be completed in several hours, with each story lasting between fifteen and thirty minutes. The brevity of each piece ensures that the emotional impact never overstays its welcome, yet collectively the stories create a satisfying sense of continuity—a reminder of how Clannad’s ensemble cast forms a tapestry of intersecting lives. Each story may be small on its own, but together they form a chorus of affection, regret, and growth that extends the emotional reach of the original narrative.

Ultimately, Clannad Side Stories is not a work that seeks to innovate but one that seeks to preserve. It is a quiet celebration of a world that has already left an indelible mark on the hearts of visual novel readers. Through its modest presentation, heartfelt voice acting, and lovingly written short tales, it succeeds in rekindling the feelings that defined Clannad’s legacy—love, family, friendship, and the beauty of fleeting moments. It is best experienced not as a standalone story but as a coda, a reflective afterword to a masterpiece that shaped an era of storytelling. For those who have laughed and cried with these characters before, returning to their world through Clannad Side Stories feels like stepping back into a familiar light—a brief, tender reunion with the warmth of memory.

I'm only 30 minutes in, but I HAVE to leave a review because of how many things this VN gets wrong. Especially after how fantastic the original VN was. 
I have 3 major problems with this game as a VN:

1. There is absolutely nothing to distinguish any of the dialogue. No varied fonts, no bold or italicizing, not even Quotations Marks to separate what's being spoken. So narration, inner thoughts, and dialogue are all exactly the same, even between different characters, having to rely on voice acting to even tell who is speaking. Something that the original VN excelled at.

2. There is no way to advance dialogue. Even if you have the text set to instant, it doesn't move along until the voice acting is finished. And it also moves along whether you are finished reading or not. You are stuck at the pace the game has decided on. Once again, something the original allowed you to decide on.

3. For the majority the time, there are no character portraits on screen. Even when two or three different characters are speaking, you better have their voices memorized. Very lovely art does pop up for each chapter, but its not always up and some art only lasts for a small percentage of the time the chapter lasts. I'm not sure why even just basic head pop ups couldn't be done, just to show who was currently speaking.

Adding a 4th issue because its minor, but it is still so silly. No save feature at all. The stories are quite short (around 20-30 minutes maybe) and there chapter selects for each story that breaks them down to let you start from specific spots, but I can not understand why we can not just save & load from anywhere. 

As far as I know, the stories are fine, most filler side content for folks who want more interactions. This review is based purely on how it operates as a visual novel and it utterly failed in my opinion. Not only did the original get all of this right, but I've played free VNs that have this all done correctly. I am simply baffled by this game.

Edited to fix grammar errors. The stories are nice, but the set up is still needlessly annoying.

[h1]碎碎念：关于clannad，关于side stories，关于麻枝准，关于创作[/h1]
五天前，早上7点17分。当我熬夜完成Clannad的长文后，瘫坐在椅子上长舒了一口气。老实讲，这篇文章在现在的我看来已经充满缺憾了。和以往不同，过于强调情感总感觉不过是把作品以自己的形式复述一遍，而最后的表达部分也因为熬夜导致并没有写的很详细很易懂，反倒是已一种相当模糊的形式表达了些我自己都不知道在写什么的内容。不过，或许心态确实改变了吧，我想，这样就好。最原本的状态，最原始的状态，即便不包含足够多的理念关联，却也饱含了我自身对于这部作品全部的感受，这就够了。

在体验side stories所有的故事后，我想，独属于我clannad的旅程也该告一段落了。如果让我用一个词语来形容这部side stories的话，那一定是“轻松”。一些足以让你褪去本篇后日谈中那样大起大落的情绪，回归到“享受”这个状态。在这部作品里，你能看到古河渚在和朋也相遇之前是如何鼓起勇气的；风子和公子独特的日常相处方式；智代的过往（感觉应该和智代After相关）；曾经在足球场上奔跑的春原；秋生和早苗的初遇；琴美后续的故事；宫泽哥哥灵异事件（bushi）；美佐枝小姐与芳野哥的恋爱故事（公子老师感觉要炸了）；幸村老师的过往和学生的信件；棒球队再集合和泡澡事件以及汐的出发。


在经历以上冗长水字数的报菜名后终于要进入正题了，可能有人发现了我并没有写藤林姐妹和柊胜平的故事，主要是我要在这里将本篇评价没有吐槽的柊胜平狠狠吐槽一下，可以说是为了为了一碟醋包一顿饺子。看完故事后我们能够知道为何藤林杏和藤林椋为何在一开始对朋也的好感度就如此之高，同时也让我不得不发个牢骚，本篇的柊胜平线实在是个比较大的败笔，莫名产生的感情以及莫名出现类似“傻白甜”人设的人物，以及side stories里面本以为会讲结果没讲的胜平当时对椋到底说了啥，都让我对这条线充满了怨念。看完椋的补充故事后一方面感叹打不过杏的确是板上钉钉的事另一方面就让我这个没啥文笔的乐色来给麻枝准提供另外一个写椋线的思路吧。给个契机让朋也问椋为什么喜欢他然后串联到这个事件作为椋线的进入点，然后朋也的迷茫同样描写出来，不过这条线让他意识到椋平时对他的一些细节然后喜欢上椋（当然前面要给椋再加些事件），最后的落点落在并不是我知道以前你替代杏和我经历的事从而喜欢上你的，我喜欢的是现在的椋作为结尾和升华表达，应该勉强可以算得上是一条合格的线了（bushi)。

在吐槽完柊胜平后，感觉一切有关clannad这两部作品的遗憾已经消失殆尽了，似乎也到了要结尾的时候了，那就来聊聊麻子吧。麻枝准对于自己创作的目的是相当清楚的。”我想创造一种能让人们心中一生难忘，在某个瞬间偶然想起的故事。如果不能做到这一点，我就觉得自己没有作为人类存在的价值了。那么，什么样的故事才是好的呢？我认为必须是具有冲击力、惊喜，或是无人经历过的独特故事。”（来源自RealSound Tech采访麻枝准）如此可见，麻枝的作品是在追求可感性的同时让玩家从反思性价值向情感性价值迁移，而正是这样的可感性，让玩家有了“仅停留在模糊感受中”的可能。这样的可能使得麻枝准能够完成他的目标“我一直在想如何用锋利的刀刺入对方的心。“这样一来麻子写作风格形成的原因也就可以理解了，为了让自己的创作刻在人们心中。”从小学时代起，我一直只追求与创作相关的东西，我想未来也是如此。“当访谈者提及50岁的他今后想如何燃尽自己的人生时，他如此说道。同样，我想将最后这半句话送给仍然在创作的所有人，无论为了何种原因，何种想法，请继续下去。或许你的创作无法被人看到，但是，没关系，你所创作的内容仍然会成为你存在最为确凿的证明。

说实话，外传从游戏性的角度是完全不推荐的，不能回看历史对话，不能中途保存（不过每一章节都挺短的，算是间接的解决了这个问题(?)），可以说是集百家之短了，哪哪都不舒服。
剧情大概只有8个小时（别问为什么我时长为什么这么长，在椅子上坐久了累了呗），16个大章节每个半小时差不多吧大概，有前传性质的（讲nagisa和tomoya的（nagisa可爱捏）），有后传性质的（和琴美的约会之类的），有完善本体伏笔的（美佐枝和拓介的），有福利的（泡温泉回（好耶））。而且其cg画面比之本体可以说的惊艳了（是我连续玩100小时cl改变了我的审美吗）。

总而言之，cl外传内容其实是匮乏的，更多的是粉丝向吧大概。
